title: signals.json: header of signals.bin, the raw per-frame signals (layer L0 of panorama.content/0)
description: signals.bin is one flat binary file of columns, each n_frames values long (rows of `width` values for vector columns), little-endian, each column starting at its `offset` (a multiple of 8) and packed without gaps inside. Row i is frame i of the frame table in presentation order; the columns pts and key ARE the frame table (see common.schema.json for the rule that turns pts into seconds). The file is created at its final size by the pre-scan and filled by the scan; the column `scanned` is 1 on a frame once the scan has written its signals (everything else is zero until then). A pair signal at row i (motion group) describes the step from frame i-1 to frame i; row 0 holds zeros. Per-frame cost is about 55 bytes. KNOWN COLUMNS (group): pts i8 ticks, key u1 (frame-table); scanned u1 (scan); tn_single f2, tn_many f2 (shots: TransNetV2 single-frame and many-hot head probabilities); scd f2, luma_mean u1, luma_p95 u1, luma_std u1, pc_peak u1, dx f4, dy f4, diff_before f2, diff_after f2, explained u1, static u1, other u1 (motion: camera-slide measurement of the step, brightness of the 480x270 luma, scdet-like cut score; luma values are the stream's own 8-bit code values, HDR is not converted, so a planner converts code values to nits with the transfer function in file-facts.json); crop_rect i2[4], bars_valid u1 (crop: cropdetect's first and last non-black column and row of the full-size frame, valid on every scanned frame and on the keyframes of the pre-scan); edge_top, edge_bottom, edge_left, edge_right u2 (bars-text: distance in source pixels from each frame edge to the first line holding two bright pixels; the scan depth, a quarter of the dimension, when none); dv_scene_refresh u1 (dolby-vision, only for Dolby Vision files).

width.description: Values per frame; more than 1 for vector columns (crop_rect has 4).

offset.description: Byte offset of the column in signals.bin; n_frames * width * itemsize bytes follow.

groups.description: Analyzer version of each signal group. A stored file is reused only when the columns and these versions match the current analyzer's.
